question: What is the primary clinical risk of leaving suture material in place longer than necessary?
explanation: Sutures act as foreign bodies that can harbor bacteria over time, making prolonged retention a primary risk factor for wound tract infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why must sutures be removed before complete epithelialization around the thread occurs?

options.A: To prevent painful removal and scarring
options.B: To speed up the systemic inflammatory response
options.C: To prevent the sutures from dissolving prematurely
options.D: To allow the surgeon to re-suture the area

explanation: When epithelium grows around the suture material, pulling it out causes unnecessary trauma, pain, and worse cosmetic scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Facial sutures are typically removed after how many days?
explanation: The face has an abundant blood supply enabling rapid healing, and early removal prevents permanent cross-hatch scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: A patient had a deep laceration repaired over the knee joint ten days ago. What is the most appropriate nursing action regarding suture removal?

options.A: Delay removal and consult the prescriber
options.B: Remove half the sutures and leave the rest for a week
options.C: Soak the knee in warm water and pull all sutures out
options.D: Remove the sutures immediately as ten days has passed

explanation: Joints experience high physical tension and slower healing, often requiring 10 to 14 days or longer before sutures can be safely removed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: What finding contraindicates the immediate removal of sutures during pre-assessment?

options.A: A slight itching sensation reported by the patient
options.B: Mild bruising around the surgical site
options.C: Incomplete wound closure or gaping edges
options.D: Dry brown crusting along the incision line

explanation: If the wound edges have not fully healed and still gape, removing sutures will cause wound dehiscence. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the correct action if a nurse discovers localized purulent drainage and wound separation during pre-assessment?

options.A: Remove all sutures to let the pus drain out freely
options.B: Apply adhesive strips directly over the pus
options.C: Leave the sutures in place and notify the prescriber
options.D: Scrub the wound vigorously with povidone-iodine

explanation: Purulent drainage combined with separation indicates infection and compromised healing, requiring medical evaluation before any sutures are disturbed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which instrument is specifically designed to slide beneath a suture thread during removal?

options.A: Scissors with a small hooked notch

explanation: Suture scissors feature a small curved hook or notch that slides easily under the thread to lift and cut it safely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why is normal saline or an appropriate antiseptic used to clean the suture line prior to removal?

options.A: To numb the superficial nerve endings in the skin
options.B: To remove surface crusts and microorganisms
options.C: To chemically dissolve the underlying suture knot
options.D: To permanently seal the epidermal wound margins

explanation: Cleaning clears away dried blood, crusts, and surface bacteria so they are not pulled down into the wound tract during removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: When cutting an interrupted suture, why should the nurse pull the cut thread in the direction of the wound?

options.A: To ensure the knot remains attached to the forceps
options.B: To prevent placing stress on the healing incision line
options.C: To push the remaining thread deeper into the subcutaneous tissue
options.D: To stretch the skin and make the removal completely painless

explanation: Pulling toward the wound pushes the edges together rather than pulling them apart, protecting the delicate new tissue from reopening. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is a major error to avoid when removing any type of suture?

options.A: Cleaning the wound surface with normal saline before cutting
options.B: Using sterile forceps to lift the knot away from the skin
options.C: Pulling the exposed external part of the thread back through the tissue
options.D: Cutting only one side of the suture loop before pulling

explanation: The portion of the suture outside the skin collects bacteria; pulling it through the tissue tract introduces those contaminants directly into the wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What simple material is often applied across an incision after suture removal to provide extra mechanical support?
explanation: Adhesive strips help bridge the wound margins and support the tissue while collagen remodeling continues after sutures are gone. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What instruction is most important for a patient immediately following suture removal?

options.A: Keep the wound clean and dry for the next day or two
options.B: Apply an antiseptic ointment and cover with a heavy occlusive seal
options.C: Return to heavy weightlifting exercises to test the wound
options.D: Apply vigorous friction massage to break down scar tissue

explanation: Keeping the area dry prevents moisture from softening the delicate new epithelial seal and inviting secondary bacterial contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the appropriate immediate nursing response if a wound begins to gape while sutures are being removed?

options.A: Quickly pull out all remaining sutures to finish the task
options.B: Suture the wound back together using a standard needle
options.C: Stop removing remaining sutures and apply adhesive strips
options.D: Leave the clinic without documenting the complication

explanation: Stopping prevents further wound disruption, and applying bridging strips supports the remaining closed margins until a clinician assesses the site. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a classic sign of localized wound infection following suture removal?

options.A: New purulent discharge along the incision
options.B: Cool, pale, and insensible skin edges
options.D: Elevated body temperature in the patient

explanation: Infection typically causes increased warmth, redness (erythema), pus, and fever rather than cool, pale skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)
